sections.title: Agriculture is everywhere
content_descriptors: Identify the characteristics and properties of food, fibre and agricultural products
Describe food and agricultural industries in New South Wales
sections.learning_intention: Explain and apply agriculture is everywhere within a resource-conscious crop-production system.
learning_sequence: Agriculture connects biological production with people, resources, processes, products and feedback. Named NSW rice and cotton examples show how grain and fibre properties, place, processing and resource constraints shape different industries.
Study the purposeful visual and use the linked media pathway: See agriculture as a changing production system, not just a paddock.
Complete the ten feedback-rich questions, revisit linked theory as needed, then save the scaffolded written response.
sections.evidence: Explain how one familiar product depends on an agricultural system rather than a single isolated action.

long_response_scaffold_prompts: What is the product's living or biological starting point?
Which important inputs and processes connect that source to the final user?
What intended and unintended outputs can you identify?
How could feedback improve one part of the system?

sections.title: First foods: plants, animals and nutrition
content_descriptors: Investigate how Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples select and use plants and animals to improve nutrition
sections.learning_intention: Explain and apply first foods: plants, animals and nutrition within a resource-conscious crop-production system.

Which resource is a plant and which is an animal, and how is its selection or use described?
What nutrition or food-availability evidence is actually published?
What local, universal or procedural claim must remain unmade?
